reranked_evidence.snippet: ## The Central District Court in Lod sentenced the defendant to 20 years and three months in prison and ordered him to pay a total of NIS 150,000 in compensation to his former wife and their daughter. The Central District Court in Lod sentenced a man to 20 years and three months in prison on Sunday for committing acts of rape and sexual assault against his three-and-a-half-year-old daughter, as well as raping his then-wife while she slept. The court sentenced him to 20 years for the offenses in the current case and ordered the consecutive activation of a three-month suspended sentence imposed in an earlier case in which he was convicted of assaulting and threatening the same woman. The prosecution asked the court to impose a total sentence of 30 years, arguing that the defendant’s admission concerning his daughter came only after he was confronted with unequivocal video evidence and that he had continued to deny and avoid responsibility for the offenses against his former wife.

Amid the #MeToo reckoning about adult abuse in the church, the Rupnik case has become one of the most sensitive matters for the Holy See, given suggestions that the priest was protected for over three decades by his Jesuit superiors and the Vatican hierarchy, up to and including the Jesuit Pope Francis. reranked_evidence.title: 3 Norwalk High softball players sue former coach accused of sexual assault - Greenwich Time
reranked_evidence.snippet: NORWALK — The families of three female teenagers are asking a court to award damages for alleged inappropriate touching and sexual assault by a former Norwalk High School softball coach who is already facing criminal charges. The lawsuit filed July 8 in Stamford/Norwalk Superior Court demands more than $15,000 in damages from Carey Nadel, 70, of Wilton, the Norwalk Board of Education and the City of Norwalk for alleged sexual assault and battery, intentional emotional distress and negligence. The plaintiffs, identified only as Jane Doe 1, 2 and 3, claim during the 2023-2024 and 2024-25 softball seasons Nadel repeatedly subjected the girls to “unwanted sexual touching of their intimate body parts, inappropriate sexual comments, and other degrading conduct.”. Nadel in May was charged with four counts of fourth-degree sexual assault and risk of injury to a child for incidents that occurred on school grounds and released after posting a $100,000 bond.
